risks.note: The lubricants industry remains exposed to fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices and competitive pricing pressures; the white mineral oils business is likewise exposed to fluctuations in feedstock costs. As a specialty petroleum manufacturer the Company's procurement cost and margin move with these inputs.
risks.risk: Crude oil, base oil and feedstock price volatility

risks.note: Management states that increasing vehicle electrification and lubricant drain intervals may gradually influence lubricant demand across certain segments, even though ICE vehicles still dominate India's automotive base and EV registrations rose around 80% in FY 2025-26.
risks.risk: Vehicle electrification and longer lubricant drain intervals

risks.note: Ester-based transformer fluids carry higher costs than conventional mineral oils and face extended qualification cycles and evolving technical standards; for new-age fluids (EV cooling, immersion cooling) commercial adoption remains dependent on technology validation, customer qualification cycles and evolving industry standards - so revenue from the ester pivot is gated by customer approval timelines.
risks.risk: Long qualification and approval cycles for new fluid technologies

risks.note: White mineral oils face evolving regulatory requirements and increasingly stringent quality standards across pharmaceutical, personal care and food-related applications; maintaining consistent product quality and compliance with global standards is stated to be critical for sustained growth.
risks.risk: Regulatory and quality-standard tightening in regulated end-uses

risks.note: In white mineral oils, competitive intensity, import pressures and shifts towards alternative ingredients in select formulations may influence market dynamics; in lubricants, competitive pricing pressure is explicitly flagged.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity, import pressure and ingredient substitution

risks.note: Changes in raw material availability and regulatory requirements may influence adoption trends of ester-based transformer fluids across certain applications.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and changing regulation for ester fluids

risks.note: BS-VI emission standards and CAFE norms continue to reshape lubricant requirements, driving a shift to low-viscosity, synthetic and semi-synthetic grades - a reformulation and requalification burden as well as a premiumisation opportunity.
risks.risk: Emission and efficiency regulation reshaping product requirements

risks.note: Handling of petroleum products requires an ISO 45001:2018-based OH&S management system, HIRA, permit-to-work, LOTO and extensive fire infrastructure (hydrant systems on dedicated 100 KL, 225 KL and 650 KL water storage tanks at 7 kg/cm2). Zero LTIFR, zero recordable injuries and zero fatalities were reported for employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.
risks.risk: Process, fire and occupational safety at manufacturing plants
